newsitem.title: USA: Lumber prices rise on anticipated cash recovery.
newsitem.headline: Lumber prices rise on anticipated cash recovery.

text.p: Lumber prices soared in light trading Friday after the Thanksgiving holiday, amid expectations that cash prices will soon recover from a severe two-week drop.
Wheat prices fell at the three U.S. major futures markets in light trading, while New York commodity markets were closed Friday in an extended holiday.
Poor exports sank corn and soybean oil futures, while forecasts for cold and snow in Texas cattle areas lifted cattle futures at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.

Cash lumber prices have gyrated sharply in recent weeks, soaring to record highs early this month when it appeared that quotas would slash Canadian shipments to the United States. But prices soon tumbled when it was apparent that builders were cutting back.

Cash lumber prices have fallen nearly $100 per 1,000 board feet since early November. Cash spruce, a key species used for wall studs in homes, went from $473 per 1,000 board feet on Nov. 15 to $378 Wednesday, according to Random Lengths, a leading lumber market service.
On Friday, CME traders bid futures higher on speculation that cash prices may rebound because of production cutbacks at lumber mills.
"A lot of (lumber) mills take down time late in the year" for the holidays, one lumber trader said.
CME January lumber finished up the $10 limit up at $392.20 per 1,000 board feet, with March up $8.20 at $378.70.
Wheat futures closed lower at the Chicago and Kansas City Boards of Trade and were mostly lower at the Minneapolis Grain Exchange led by selling in Chicago.
"Fund selling pressured wheat," said Ron Kucha, a Chicago grain trader with O'Connor & Co. "No deliveries on the (CBOT) December was a little supportive."
Also bearish was news Turkey will seek up to 200,000 metric tons of wheat beginning Dec. 10. Traders and analysts expected it to seek 500,000 metric tons.

CBOT March wheat was down 6-3/4 cents at $3.77-1/2 per bushel. Kansas City Board of Trade March wheat was off 5-3/4 cents at $3.95-1/2 and Minneapolis Grain Exchange March spring wheat was off 5-1/2 cents at $3.81-1/2.
CBOT corn futures closed slightly lower on disappointing export sales and pressure for lower wheat markets.
The Agriculture Department said Friday the United States sold 582,900 metric tons of corn during the week ended Nov. 21, which was below trade estimates of 700,000 to 900,000 tons.
CBOT March corn was down 2-1/2 cents at $2.71 per bushel.

Low soyoil exports fuelled selling in CBOT soyoil futures, which closed down 0.25 cent in December at 22.98 cents per pound. The Agriculture Department reported sales during the week ended Nov. 21 at 14,700 tons vs. expectations of 20,000 to 50,000 tons.

Cold and snow forecast for Texas cattle areas this weekend prompted buying in Chicago Mercantile Exchange live cattle futures, on ideas the stressful weather will slow weight gains in cattle and delay marketings.
CME December live cattle closed up 0.225 cent at 67.025 cents per pound.
